title: Fair Classification with Efficient and Post-hoc Controllable Fairness-Accuracy Trade-off
claim: A standard post-processing pipeline trains with ERM; ours swaps in a learned fair representation, keeping the same post-hoc controllable prediction stage.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, training/prediction zones color-coded, contrast by color
description: Two stacked flow diagrams, (a) FairBayes on top and (b) the proposed GFB below. Each has a rounded 'Training' region on the left and a green 'Prediction' region on the right. In (a) the training region is light blue. The flow runs Dataset S, then an ERM box, then the output Z_a^ERM, then a Post-process box, then the final classifier f^ERM. A long arrow carries the dataset directly to Post-process. A Constraint δ input enters Post-process from below. Panel (b) has the same layout. Its training region is red or pink, and the ERM box is replaced by a GFB box. Its outputs are Z_a^GFB and f^GFB. White boxes and parallelograms on pastel backgrounds make the changed training stage the main visual contrast.
caption: Comparison of algorithmic flows: (a) FairBayes and (b) the proposed method.
abstract: Post-hoc controllability of fair machine learning models, the ability to control the trade-off between fairness and accuracy after training, is valuable for practical deployment. Existing post-processing methods provide such post-hoc controllability but often suffer from significant accuracy degradation, whereas in-processing methods achieve efficient trade-offs but require computationally expensive retraining for each change in trade-off ratio. To achieve both post-hoc controllability and efficient trade-offs, we propose a novel fair classification algorithm that learns effective feature representations to improve the trade-off efficiency of post-processing fair classifiers, by a gradient-based optimization approach. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves trade-off efficiency comparable to, or even surpassing, in-processing methods, without requiring any retraining.
